content:
Since \(n \mid 3^n\), \(n\) must be a power of \(3\). Let \(n=3^k\), \(k\ge 1\).

The second condition is
\[
3^{3^k}\equiv 1 \pmod{3^k-1}.
\]
Because \(3^k\equiv 1 \pmod{3^k-1}\), this holds iff \(k\mid 3^k\). Thus \(k\) must also be a power of \(3\).

The first two such \(k\) are \(k=1\) and \(k=3\), giving
\[
n=3^1=3,\qquad n=3^3=27.
\]
Their sum is
\[
3+27=30.
\]

\[
\boxed{30}
\]
